gloss: passing away; being at a loss, giving up

definitions.explanation: In Buddhist terminology, departing this world to be reborn in the Pure Land. By extension, used as a euphemism for dying or passing away.

definitions.gloss: being at a loss, being stuck, giving up
definitions.explanation: Being in a helpless situation where one has no choice but to accept or give in. Often implies reluctant resignation when faced with something unavoidable.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{安|やす}らかに{往生|おうじょう}した。
{大往生|だいおうじょう}を{遂|と}げた。
examples.english: He died a peaceful death at a ripe old age.

examples.japanese: {長生|ながい}きして{大往生|だいおうじょう}できれば、それが{一番|いちばん}の{幸|しあわ}せだ。
examples.english: Living long and passing away peacefully would be the greatest happiness.

examples.japanese: あの{頑固|がんこ}さには{往生|おうじょう}した。
examples.english: I was at a complete loss with that stubbornness.

examples.japanese: {渋滞|じゅうたい}で{動|うご}けず、{往生|おうじょう}した。
examples.english: I was stuck and helpless because of the traffic jam.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まって{駅|えき}で{二時間|にじかん}も{往生|おうじょう}させられた。
examples.english: The train stopped and I was stranded at the station for two hours.

notes:
USAGE:
Originally a Buddhist term meaning rebirth in the Pure Land after death. Sense 1 remains a respectful euphemism for dying, especially a peaceful death. Sense 2 developed from the metaphorical idea of being "dead in the water" — stuck in a situation with no way out.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大往生|だいおうじょう}: peaceful death at an old age
- {往生|おうじょう}する: to pass away; to be stuck/helpless
- {往生際|おうじょうぎわ}が{悪|わる}い: to not know when to give up

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {逝去|せいきょ}: passing away (formal, honorific)
- {困|こま}る: to be troubled, at a loss (more casual, sense 2)
